newsitem.title: USA: Torchmark cash flow available for buyback.
newsitem.headline: Torchmark cash flow available for buyback.

text.p: Torchmark Corp said first quarter operating earnings from continuing operations rose 17 percent as a result of improvements in its core businesses and said improved cash flow is available to repurchase shares.
First quarter life insurance sales matched sales for the year ago quarter, but exceeded sales during the fourth quarter of 1996 by 4.5 percent, Torchmark said.

It said as expected, its LNL Exclusive Agency unit's life sales during the first quarter of 1997 were less than those of the same period of 1996. However, they increased by two percent as compared with the fourth quarter of 1996.
Increasing life production is expected to continue at Liberty National as a result of new agent recruiting efforts begun in late 1996, Torchmark said.
Medicare supplement sales fell five percent to $16.4 million in the first quarter.
Pre-tax operating income of Waddell & Reed rose 13 percent to $31 million in the first quarter, due to increased management and service fees.
Mutual fund assets under management at March 31, 1997 were $19 billion, the same as at the end of the first quarter of 1996.
Investment product collections in the first quarter fell 11 percent to $362 million compared with a year ago, Waddell & Reed's highest quarter on record for investment product collections.
However, investment product collections for the first quarter of 1997 exceeded those during the fourth quarter of 1996 by 7.5 percent.
Total Torchmark revenue for the first quarter of 1997, excluding investment realized gains and losses, was $568 million, a four percent increase compared with the same period in 1996.

Life premium revenue rose six percent to $222 million and health premium revenue was level at $188 million. Financial services revenue increased nine percent to $48 million for the quarter as compared with the first quarter of 1996.
